source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
The source describes three main propagation methods for pomelo planting material (បច្ចេកទេសរៀបចំពូជ), the same three approaches used for other Cambodian citrus crops in this knowledge base:

1. Seed propagation (ការបង្កាត់ដោយគ្រាប់) - simplest, but seedling trees vary genetically and are slow to bear fruit.
2. Air-layering/marcotting - rooting a branch while still attached to the parent tree, then cutting and planting it; reproduces the mother tree faithfully and is the method described in most detail in this source.
3. Grafting/budding onto rootstock (ដើមគល់ / Grafting) - joining a bud or scion (មេក) from a proven mother tree onto separate rootstock; recommended by extension staff, especially for producing planting stock that develops a strong root system.

The source notes that in Cambodia, marcotting is by far the most common method farmers use for pomelo, because trees grown this way begin fruiting sooner.
